chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding

A man who maroffs his slave to a free woman with a dowry of one hundred dirhams, then sells him before entering (consummating marriage) with her, he said: 'Her master gives her from the sale price half of what he fixed for her; for it is in the position of a debt that he borrowed on her master's command.'
And it is not permissible for the slave to contract marriage with more than two free women or four slave women.
52. That was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the slave who marries four free women, he said: 'No, but he marries two free women, and if he wishes, he marries four slave women.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave's wife if he is sold before consummation, and how many wives can a slave have?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of a slave's marriage by treating the dowry as a debt owed by the master, ensuring the free wife's financial security upon the slave's sale. It further refines the jurisprudential distinction regarding polygamy, explicitly permitting a slave to marry up to four slave women or two free women, reflecting the economic and social constraints of the era.
